title: Altering Cadence or Vertical Oscillation During Running: Effects on Running Related Injury Factors
publisher: International Journal of Sports Physical Therapy
claims: In 20 active runners, a high-cadence condition reduced ground contact time by 4.7%, while a low-oscillation cue increased ground contact time by 3.5%.
High cadence reduced average vertical loading rate by 21.2% and instantaneous vertical loading rate by 16.0%.
The low-oscillation condition reduced average vertical loading rate by 33.4% and also reduced instantaneous vertical loading rate (p=0.001).
Only the high-cadence condition significantly reduced braking impulse.
Cadence, vertical oscillation and ground contact time were calculated using the proprietary Garmin Connect algorithm.
The study measured loading factors linked to injury risk, not running performance or running economy.
